_note: Published power and performance figures used to CALIBRATE the 'today' profile and the audit of the overview note (October 2026). 'status': confirmed = read in a primary or vendor source during the audit; confirmed_secondary = only repeated by secondary coverage; unconfirmed = not found; discrepancy = sources disagree. 'kind' says what the number is: rating / maximum / average / reported. These are MIXED quantities and not matched benchmarks; a model-to-reference ratio is a sanity check, not a validation.

helios_base_unit.label: Quantinuum Helios (98 qubits), base unit without support infrastructure
helios_base_unit.kind: rating (vendor page: 'less than 40kW', footnote 'Valid for the base unit without support infrastructure')
helios_base_unit.note: The overview's 'less than 40 kW' is correct as an upper bound, but it omits that the Oracle/Quantinuum announcement reports about 60 kW (see helios_oracle).

helios_oracle.label: Quantinuum Helios in Oracle OCI, 'roughly 60 kW without its HVAC system'
helios_oracle.note: DISCREPANCY with the <40 kW page: scope differs ('base unit' versus the installation), neither is a metered average. The overview does not mention the 60 kW figure.

dwave_advantage2.label: D-Wave Advantage2 annealing system
dwave_advantage2.kind: 'Average power 12.5 kW' on the data sheet; rating 208 V 60 A (standard) / 230/400 V 32 A (international)
dwave_advantage2.note: 208 V x 60 A = 12.5 kVA, so the figure may coincide with the circuit rating rather than a metered average. D-Wave claims constant power over six generations (vendor claim).

quandela_ascella.label: Quandela Ascella (6 qubits), main system
quandela_ascella.kind: vendor figure ('3 kW'); an independent review says 'under 3 kW on 220 V AC'
quandela_ascella.boundary: system incl. its compact cryostat built into the rack
quandela_ascella.source: Quandela product page and Oct 2025 whitepaper; arXiv:2409.08229
quandela_ascella.note: 6-qubit machine delivered 2022, not a fault-tolerant system. Search did not surface the page text directly; the 3 kW figure was confirmed through the search summaries of the product page, whitepaper and review.

pasqal_overview.label: Pasqal neutral-atom machine, 'about 2.6 kW'
pasqal_overview.kind: secondary article (MarketScreener) says 'approximately 2.6 kW' for the current processor
pasqal_overview.source: sa.marketscreener.com (secondary); NOT in Pasqal's own brochure
pasqal_overview.note: Pasqal's September 2024 presentation gave 3 kW for Fresnel (search snippet). The December 2025 brochure lists a class IV laser of '10 kW (3.5 kW on average during operation)' alone, which already exceeds 2.6 kW. Treat 2.6 kW as an older or partial figure.

pasqal_brochure.label: Pasqal quantum computer brochure Dec 2025: laser and supply
pasqal_brochure.kind: average laser power; installed laser 10 kW; supply '1x three-phase 380 V 32 A' (about 21 kVA connection, a rating)
pasqal_brochure.note: Also lists a water-cooling inlet/outlet, 9 modules, 4,000 kg, operating at room temperature.

quera_aquila_paqit.label: QuEra Aquila as modelled in PaQit: P = 6.92 kW + 0.308 W/qubit
quera_aquila_paqit.kind: model parameters fitted by the PaQit authors to QuEra data (~7 kW at 256 qubits, ~10 kW at 10,000 qubits)
quera_aquila_paqit.boundary: system (as reported by QuEra via the authors)
quera_aquila_paqit.source: arXiv:2608.02815 (Ludmir & Patel), section VI-A; text extracted 2026-10-18
quera_aquila_paqit.note: The authors state these values characterise relative scheduling behaviour, not absolute device power.

dgx_b200.label: NVIDIA DGX B200 (8 GPUs)
dgx_b200.kind: '14.3 kW max.'; six 3.3 kW PSUs in 5+1 redundancy; per-GPU maximum 1,000 W with five PSUs
dgx_b200.source: NVIDIA DGX B200 user guide, read 2026-10-18
dgx_b200.note: The guide's power table labels the 14.3 kW row 'Specification for Each Power Supply', which is ambiguous; the system reading is the usual one and is repeated by third-party datasheet mirrors.

mi350x.label: AMD Instinct MI350X
mi350x.source: AMD announcement coverage via search (multiple agreeing sources)

mi355x.label: AMD Instinct MI355X
mi355x.source: AMD announcement coverage via search (multiple agreeing sources)

mlperf_llama2_70b.label: AMD MI355X, MLPerf Inference 6.0, Llama 2 70B, single node (8 GPUs), Server scenario
mlperf_llama2_70b.kind: AMD-reported throughput, not an energy measurement, not independently reproduced
mlperf_llama2_70b.source: AMD ROCm blog / AMD blog (via search); MLCommons results published 2026-04-01

helios_below_40kw.claim: Quantinuum Helios less than 40 kW (base unit, support excluded)
helios_below_40kw.verdict: confirmed, but incomplete: Oracle announcement says about 60 kW excluding HVAC

dwave_12_5kw.verdict: confirmed (data sheet: average power 12.5 kW); equals 208 V x 60 A, may be a rating

quandela_ascella_3kw.verdict: confirmed (vendor); includes its built-in cryostat; 6-qubit system

pasqal_2_6kw.claim: Historical Pasqal neutral-atom machine about 2.6 kW
pasqal_2_6kw.verdict: NOT confirmed from a primary source; one secondary article; Pasqal's 2024 slide says 3 kW and its 2025 brochure lists 3.5 kW average laser power alone

dgx_b200_14_3kw.claim: DGX B200 up to 14.3 kW (complete server)
dgx_b200_14_3kw.verdict: confirmed (NVIDIA guide '14.3 kW max', table header ambiguous)

mi355x_1_4kw.claim: MI355X up to 1.4 kW; MI350X 1.0 kW; eight MI355X 11.2 kW
mi355x_1_4kw.verdict: confirmed via agreeing secondary coverage; arithmetic correct

mlperf_97_100_119.claim: MI355X ~100 % / 97 % / 119 % of B200 (Offline / Server / Interactive), Llama 2 70B
mlperf_97_100_119.verdict: confirmed as AMD's own single-node comparison; not independently reproduced; throughput only

quantum_echoes_13000x.claim: Google Quantum Echoes ~13,000x vs classical, ~2 hours on Willow
quantum_echoes_13000x.verdict: confirmed as Google's claim (about 2.1 h vs an estimated 3.2 years on Frontier; Nature, Oct 2025); baseline is an estimate, not an energy comparison; 65 qubits used per coverage

ibm_nighthawk.verdict: confirmed: 120-qubit square-lattice processor announced Nov 2025 with Loon; Starling 2029 (200 logical, 1e8 gates) and Blue Jay 2033+ (2,000 logical, 1e9 gates) are company targets

atom_ac1000.verdict: confirmed on the company site (1,200+ qubits, on-premises)

oxford_ionics.verdict: partly confirmed: IonQ acquired Oxford Ionics in June 2025 (single secondary source in this audit)

quantum_circuits_dwave.verdict: partly confirmed: D-Wave announced an agreement to acquire it for about USD 550 million in January 2026; closing not verified

iqm_machines.verdict: partly confirmed: Spark (5 qubits) and Radiance (54 qubits, delivery planned June 2026) found; Garnet (20 qubits) only in an older cloud-service report; IQM also announced Halocene (150 qubits, end of 2026)

not_checked.claim: Rigetti Cepheus, Origin Wukong, Xanadu Aurora, Intel Tunnel Falls, Diraq, Quantum Brilliance, QuEra Aquila/Gemini, Pasqal Orion, Alice & Bob Boson
not_checked.verdict: not verified individually in this audit (searches returned nothing or only unrelated pages); Majorana 1 is announced as an 8-qubit topological chip
